title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 1, Fugue 15 in G major

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 9–10) in part, with the soprano's line in the alto, the alto's line in the bass, transposed. Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from the subject. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted and a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Returns in Episode 3 (bars 46–50).
sections.leads: Between two statements in G major

sections.label: Subject in G major, inverted (Alto); Subject in D major, inverted (Soprano); Subject in G major, inverted (Bass)
Episode 2
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 9–10) in part, with the alto's line in the bass, at the same pitch level. Soprano: a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar.
sections.leads: From G major to E minor

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 9–10), with soprano and alto exchanged, transposed. Soprano: a figure from the subject. Alto: free counterpoint.
sections.leads: Between two statements in E minor

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 1 (bars 15–19) in part, with soprano and alto exchanged, a third higher. Soprano: a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from the subject and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted and the opening of the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar.
sections.leads: From E minor to B minor

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in B minor, rhythm varied (Soprano); Subject in B minor (Bass)
Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted and a figure from the subject, inverted and a figure from countersubject 1. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar.
sections.leads: From B minor to D major

sections.label: Stretto: Subject in D major (Alto); Subject in D major (Soprano)
Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from countersubject 1 (3 times) and a figure from the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1 (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar.
sections.leads: From D major to G major; perfect cadence in D major at bar 69

sections.label: Episode 6
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (3 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence falling by a third every bar. Alto: the opening of the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every half bar. Bass: a figure from the subject (5 times) and the opening of the subject, inverted.
sections.leads: Between two statements in G major

sections.label: Episode 7
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject and a figure from countersubject 1. Alto: free counterpoint. Bass: free counterpoint.
sections.leads: Perfect cadence in G major at bar 83

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted. Alto: a figure from the subject and a figure from countersubject 1, inverted. Returns in Episode 1 (bars 15–19). Returns in Episode 2 (bars 31–37). Returns in Link (bar 42).
